title: Testing before launch, watching after
hook: Vibe check, golden questions, judge models, traces. How you know it is good and stays good.

useCase.title: The boss asks: "How do we know the bot is good, and staying good?"
useCase.story: ShopEase launched the assistant with RAG and tools. Models, documents and customers keep changing.

approaches.name: Vibe check
approaches.what: Try a few chats and see how they feel.

approaches.name: Golden question set
approaches.what: 50 to 200 real questions with known good answers, re-run after every change.
approaches.example: "Return window for opened electronics?" must say 14 days.

approaches.name: A model as judge
approaches.what: Another model grades answers against the sources and your rules.
approaches.greatWhen: Checking many answers, tone, and whether claims are supported.
approaches.avoidWhen: As the only check. Judges have biases, so spot-check with people.
approaches.example: "Is every claim supported by the cited passage?"

approaches.name: Separate search and answer scores
approaches.what: Score the search (did we find the right passage?) apart from the writing (did we use it faithfully?).
approaches.greatWhen: RAG and agents. It shows where things broke.
approaches.example: The search score dropped after a new PDF import.

approaches.name: Live traces and feedback
approaches.what: Log every step, collect thumbs up and down, review bad chats weekly.
approaches.example: A dashboard: 4% thumbs-down, mostly on warranty questions.

challenge.question: Which combination catches problems before and after launch?

options.text: A vibe check on the demo
options.why: It misses the cases that matter and cannot detect drift.

options.text: A golden set, separate search and answer scores, a judge model, and live traces
options.why: It catches problems before launch, pinpoints where they come from, and keeps watching afterwards.
You find out late, from your angriest users.
Useful, but it needs a real question set and human spot-checks.

bestCase.title: Test before every change, trace after launch
bestCase.example: A new PDF import lowers the search score from 92% to 71% overnight. The dashboard points at chunking, not the model. You fix it in an hour, before customers notice.

worstCase.title: "It looked fine in the demo"
worstCase.example: There is no test set and no logs. The bot quotes an outdated warranty for weeks. You learn about it from a social media post, and cannot tell which change caused it.

route.travelling: Golden question: "Return window for opened electronics?"

steps.label: Run the bot
steps.goes: Answers and retrieved passages are recorded for every question.
steps.goesWrong: There is no test set. Nobody runs anything after the update.

steps.label: Score search and answers
steps.goes: The search score is 71%, down from 92%.

steps.label: Fix and re-test
steps.goes: Chunking is fixed and the score returns to 92%.

steps.label: Live traces and thumbs
steps.goes: Real chats keep feeding new test cases.

takeaway: You cannot improve what you do not measure, and models, documents and customers all change.
